concepts.label: Vaccines prepare the immune system before infection
quotes: A vaccine prepares the immune system to recognise a germ before a real infection happens.
showing the body an antigen

concepts.label: Antigens are foreign molecules recognized by the immune system
quotes: an antigen, which is a molecule the immune system can recognise as foreign.
Most antigens used in vaccines are proteins or sugars

concepts.label: B cells make antibodies
quotes: B cells produce antibodies, which are proteins that attach to a specific antigen
mark it for destruction

concepts.label: Helper and killer T cells have different roles
quotes: helper T cells coordinate the response by sending chemical signals
killer T cells destroy body cells that have already been infected

concepts.label: Antigen-presenting cells display antigens to T cells
quotes: Antigen-presenting cells, such as dendritic cells, capture antigens and display them to T cells.

concepts.label: Steps of the immune response after vaccination
quotes: After vaccination, the response follows a set order.
First, the vaccine introduces the antigen into the body.
Finally, some B and T cells remain as memory cells

concepts.label: Memory cells provide a faster later response
quotes: some B and T cells remain as memory cells, ready to respond quickly to the same germ later.

concepts.label: Protection takes about two weeks and may need a booster
quotes: It usually takes about two weeks after vaccination for the body to build protection.
Some vaccines need a second dose, called a booster

concepts.label: Main vaccine types
quotes: There are four main types of vaccine covered in these notes: live-attenuated vaccines, inactivated vaccines, subunit vaccines and mRNA vaccines.

concepts.label: Live-attenuated vaccines contain weakened germs
quotes: Live-attenuated vaccines contain a weakened form of the germ.

concepts.label: Inactivated vaccines contain killed germs
quotes: Inactivated vaccines contain a germ that has been killed.

concepts.label: Subunit vaccines contain selected pieces of the germ
quotes: Subunit vaccines contain only selected pieces of the germ, such as one protein.

concepts.label: mRNA vaccines instruct cells to make a harmless piece of protein
quotes: mRNA vaccines contain instructions that tell the body's own cells to make a harmless piece of the germ's protein.

concepts.label: Antibiotics are not vaccines
quotes: Antibiotics are not vaccines at all: they are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing

concepts.label: Herd immunity protects people who cannot be vaccinated
quotes: When enough people in a community are immune, a germ struggles to spread from person to person.
This indirect protection is called herd immunity
